title: Investment in the Contract When a Held Survivor Share Is Released — Income Annuities Tax Note
content:
The tax-free part of a survivor share released from an installment held on an Ashgrove Income Annuities contract is never more than the investment in the contract less the tax-free amount already recovered and never less than zero, so that once the investment is recovered the whole released share is taxable. For these contracts the investment in the contract is fixed as stated:

- **Contract bought by annuitizing an Ashgrove deferred fixed annuity or an Ashgrove fixed indexed annuity** — the cost basis of the annuity annuitized, read from the record of that Deferred Fixed Annuities or Fixed Indexed Annuities contract (the income contract record names the annuitized contract and shows the purchase source).
- **Any other traditional or SEP IRA contract** — zero.

An Income Annuities contract in neither situation is outside this rule.

**Examples (hypothetical released share $1,000.00, exclusion ratio 45%).**

1. Annuitized SecureRate contract, Deferred Fixed Annuities cost basis $150,000.00, already recovered $149,800.00: room $200.00; the share multiplied by 45% is $450.00, more than the room, so the tax-free part is $200.00; taxable $800.00.
2. Annuitized IncomeShield contract, Fixed Indexed Annuities cost basis $150,000.00, already recovered $20,000.00: tax-free part $450.00; taxable $550.00.
3. Traditional IRA from an IRA rollover: investment zero; the whole $1,000.00 is taxable.
